author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell calls out what he sees happening to Christianity in England, a faith reduced to something grey, dull, and tepid, the kind you'd nervously slip into rather than something that sets you on fire. He's careful to praise the brilliant people within the Church of England who've taught him since coming to faith, but insists the overall presentation has lost something essential. Reading from Genesis to Revelation, he argues, reveals fire, power, and angels, a stark contrast to the watered down version most people encounter, and a reminder that real faith was never meant to be boring.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Chris Pratt gets refreshingly honest about his friendship with Bobby Kennedy Jr, admitting he doesn't grill him on policy over dinner and mostly just wishes him well. But he draws a clear line on one thing, getting toxic ingredients out of kids' food is objectively good, no matter who's behind it. He pushes back hard on the instinct to reject something purely because of who proposed it, joking he'd rather put bleach in his own children's cereal himself than admit the administration got something right. It's a rare moment of someone refusing to let politics override common sense.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest draws a striking connection to why 9/11 still unsettles people, not the act itself, but the terrifying clarity of a belief system so strong someone would die for it. He turns that into a call to spiritual detachment, urging listeners not to grip too tightly to this temporary world or make it their god, because it will always let them down. But once someone truly repents and turns away from the world's counterfeit promises, he argues, they become something far more dangerous, a person the system can no longer control.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest presses RFK Jr. directly on aerosol injections containing bromine, aluminum, and strontium, sprayed into the skies daily, and demands to know how to stop it. RFK insists his own agency has nothing to do with it, naming DARPA and jet fuel emissions as the real source, and vows to do everything in his power to put a stop to it. What makes the exchange land hardest is his own admission, that even if this were happening, there's no way for the public to actually know for certain, yet he still believes it probably is.
